links.outcome: Comparison of 12 candidate open-source LLMs on same annotated data to select configuration
links.effect: Qwen3-8b no-role macro F1 0.89 vs Llama3.1-8b 0.35-0.40 and Llama2-Chinese-7b 0.00-0.11; model choice greatly affected performance.
links.quote: Among all configurations, Qwen3-8b with no-role prompting achieved a macro F 1 -score of 0.89 and balanced accuracy of 0.95±0.06, with an inference time of 3.64 seconds per record, whereas Qwen3-1.7b under zero-shot prompting achieved a macro F 1 -score of 0.85 with a faster inference time of 1.61 seconds.

links.outcome: Inter-rater agreement of independent annotators establishing the reference standard
links.effect: Two independent trained raters; symptom-specific Cohen kappa 0.87 to 1.00, overall mean 0.92 (SD 0.02); discrepancies resolved by consensus adjudication.
links.quote: Symptom-specific Cohen κ ranged from 0.87 to 1.00.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of LLM performance to prompt variation across models
links.effect: Effect of prompting strategy was model-dependent; e.g., Qwen3-1.7b macro F1 0.63 (no-role) vs 0.85 (zero-shot); Qwen3-8b 0.89 no-role vs 0.78 zero-shot.
links.quote: The effect of prompting strategy was model-dependent, and no single approach dominated across all models.

links.outcome: Extraction performance by symptom prevalence (rare vs common symptoms)
links.effect: Nausea F1 below 0.5 for all models except two under few-shot; diarrhea F1>0.8 for most models; rarer symptoms had greater variability.
links.quote: The most challenging symptom was nausea, with F 1 -scores below 0.5 for all models except Qwen3-8b and Qwen3-1.7b under few-shot prompting.

links.outcome: Generalizability of LLM performance beyond single-site Chinese chief complaints
links.effect: No external validation; results may not extend to non-Chinese EHRs, other institutions, or other symptom categories.
links.quote: First, the absence of external validation across different clinical settings or languages constrains the conclusions about model generalizability.
